extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary); patent practitioners and applicants (secondary)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing a patent application for allowance and for completing the post-allowance/issue steps (examiner actions, amendments, notices, searches, printing, and quality review) at the USPTO. Covers substantive and formal checks, examiner’s amendments, reasons for allowance, interference searches, issue processing, and related procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantially Allowable Application — special handling
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is in condition for allowance, except as to matters of form, the application will be considered special and prompt action taken to require correction of formal matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 710.02(b). If only formal defects remain, treat as special for prompt correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whole-application review for allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: Before allowance, the examiner must review the entire application to ensure it meets all formal and substantive (statutory) requirements and that claim language is enabled by and has adequate descriptive support in the originally filed disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neglect may lead to confusion as to scope. Ensure clear support/antecedent basis for terminology used in claims. Exact terms need not appear verbatim but substantial correspondence is required (37 CFR 1.121(e)). See cited case law (Eiselstein v. Frank; In re Wertheim) and MPEP §§ 608.01(o), 608.01(j), 608.01(n).

rubrics_metrics.name: Antecedent basis and terminology consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be clear support or antecedent basis in the specification for terminology used in the claims; amending/adding terms not appearing in the specification can create uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that claim terms track the specification; avoid introducing unsupported special definitions. See MPEP § 608.01(o).

rubrics_metrics.name: Renumber claims per regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims should be renumbered as required by 37 CFR 1.126 and dependent-claim numbering must be consistent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay particular attention to dependent claims that refer to previous claims; see MPEP § 608.01(j) and § 608.01(n).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract must provide an adequate and clear statement of the disclosed invention and be limited to 150 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should check the abstract and, if they change it by examiner’s amendment, follow MPEP § 1302.04 guidance. Point out defects in the first Office action or as early as possible so the applicant can correct them. Abstract may be used to determine claim meaning (case law cited).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The title may not exceed 500 characters and must be as short and specific as possible; it should be descriptive of the invention claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant's title is unsatisfactory, the examiner may require a change on or after allowance. See 37 CFR 1.72 and MPEP §§ 606, 606.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: All amendments should be reviewed to ensure they were timely filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure compliance with applicable time limits and statutes; untimely amendments may affect allowance or patent term adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for a rewritten specification
rubrics_metrics.description: When interlineations or cancellations in the specification or amendments would lead to confusion or mistake, the examiner should require the affected portion to be rewritten before passing the application to issue (37 CFR 1.125).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 13.01 and specify the sections to be rewritten. See MPEP § 608.01(q) and form paragraph notes for substitute specifications (form paragraph 6.28.01).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Allowability (PTOL-37)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use PTOL-37 whenever an application has been placed in condition for allowance; include the date of communications/interviews that resulted in allowance and notify applicant promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt notice can avoid unnecessary appeals and safeguard against abandonment. See MPEP § 714.13 and § 1302.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on examiner corrections to written record
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may not make corrections/interlineations in the body of written portions of the specification or other papers except via examiner’s amendment approved by applicant, except for enumerated exceptions (A–F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.121. Exceptions include: (A) renumbering claims (37 CFR 1.126); (B) correcting erroneous citations on IDS; (C) correcting non-compliant 1.312 amendments whose entry would otherwise be recommended; (D) canceling non-elected claims (no traverse) not eligible for rejoinder; (E) amending title to correspond with claim when Office has established title; (F) amendment/cancellation of claims following PTAB decisions (MPEP §§ 1214, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Image file wrapper applications — no informal examiner amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Informal examiner’s amendments are not permitted in image file wrapper applications; any correction must be by examiner’s amendment or applicant amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to image file wrapper applications must follow examiner’s amendment procedures or applicant-submitted amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling parent references for continuing applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For continuing applications filed under 37 CFR 1.53(b), a parent-application reference in the first sentence of the specification is no longer required if the reference is in the Application Data Sheet; the examiner should not add such a reference without applicant approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify Applicant Data Sheet accuracy; applicant may delete benefit claim; petition under 37 CFR 1.78 may be required for unintentionally delayed benefit claims for certain filings. See MPEP § 211.04 and § 601.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s amendment procedures and authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner’s amendment must be signed by the primary examiner, entered into the file, and a copy sent to applicant. Determine if an extension of time is required for entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include form paragraphs 13.02 and 13.02.01 (and 13.02.02 if an extension is required). See MPEP § 706.07(f) and form paragraph instructions; examiner’s amendments may place the application in condition for allowance but applicant may file their own amendment under 37 CFR 1.312 if changes are unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of examiner’s amendments for expediting allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.121(g) permits examiner’s amendments to make additions/deletions to the specification/claims without complying with certain 1.121(b)/(c) formalities to expedite prosecution and reduce cycle time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may instruct technical staff to make precise changes. Examiner’s amendments can correct non-compliant applicant amendments that would otherwise place the application in condition for allowance (see MPEP § 714, II.E).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s amendments by fax/email and attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: A clean-version paragraph/claim or portions submitted by applicant via fax or email (requested by examiner) may be attached and relied upon as part of an examiner’s amendment, but the attachment must be marked “requested” to avoid patent term adjustment reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Print and attach the email/fax to the examiner’s amendment; the paper copy should be entered in the file. Examiners are not required to retain electronic copies once printed. Email exceptions are limited to applicant-to-examiner emails complying with MPEP § 502.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charges via examiner’s amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner’s amendment may make charges against a deposit account or credit card to expedite issuance provided prior approval is obtained from applicant/representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record name of authorizing party, date and type of authorization, purpose for charge, and deposit account number. Credit card authorizations require a properly completed PTO-2038 fax; Office employees may not accept oral credit card instructions for certain fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive changes to abstract/specification require applicant approval
rubrics_metrics.description: No examiner’s amendment may make substantive changes to the written portions of the specification, including the abstract, without first obtaining applicant’s approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the abstract may affect claim interpretation, examiners should review and point out defects early. Case law supports that abstract can determine claim meaning (Pandrol USA; Hill-Rom).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of claims in examiner’s amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: To identify a claim in an examiner’s amendment, refer to it by the original application number and, if renumbered, by the new allowed application number as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use both numbers to avoid confusion and ensure correct indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder of claims — listing and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Previously withdrawn claims that are being rejoined and allowed must be listed in the index of claims and on the Notice of Allowability; the examiner should notify the applicant of rejoinder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to list may cause printer queries. See MPEP § 821.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of drawings when otherwise ready for issue
rubrics_metrics.description: If an allowed application requires slight drawing corrections not involving structural change, the examiner prepares a letter indicating the change and, if necessary, a marked-up drawing; drawings are then processed via Office of Data Management and FMF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If replacement drawings received are still unacceptable, mail a 'Notice to File Corrected Application Papers' giving a time period to file corrected drawings. See MPEP § 608.02(w) and (z).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference search before issue
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is in condition for allowance, an interference search must be made using the most efficient/effective manner based on the broadest claimed subject matter; consider all effective filing dates for CIPs and extend search beyond the application’s classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use text searches, classified searches, or combinations (e.g., US-PGPUB). For nucleotide/peptide claims, request STIC to perform sequence interference searches. Record the search in the file and extend search to all classes/subgroups used during examination. See MPEP §§ 2133.01, 2152.01, 719.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue Classification sheet completion and Patent Data Portal accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner preparing application for issue must complete the Issue Classification sheet and ensure prior U.S. application data (benefit claims) and provisional/foreign application data are correct in the Patent Data Portal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Patent Data Portal is not up-to-date after approved changes, forward to TC Legal Instrument Examiner with explanation. See MPEP § 202 for notations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of claim(s) and figure for Official Gazette printing
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the broadest claim for printing; ordinarily designate one claim per invention (max five if multiple inventions). Do not select a dependent claim unless its independent claim is also printed. Select a single figure consistent with the printed claim that is not labeled 'prior art'; if none, indicate 'None'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reissue, select the broadest changed or additional reissue claim. Record renumbered patent claim numbers when designating print claims. For multiple claim selections separate numbers by commas; in multiple dependent selections include the entire claim chain for one embodiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listing of references and examiner citation practices
rubrics_metrics.description: All references cited by the examiner during prosecution (including PTAB decisions and reissue oaths) must be listed on PTO-892 or an IDS and initialed; examiner-listed references on PTO-892 will be printed with an asterisk on the patent front page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical support will verify at least one reference list exists and that references on IDS are initialed or lined-through. Examiner-cited pertinent art at allowance may be listed on PTO-892 and attached to the Notice of Allowability but not sent to applicant; foreign patent docs and non-patent literature will be scanned and added to the file wrapper for applicant viewing. Erroneous citations should be corrected by examiner’s amendment (see MPEP § 707.05(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner signing and printed examiner names
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary and assistant examiners involved in allowance apply E-signatures on the Issue Classification sheet; only names appearing on that sheet will be printed in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary examiner who prepares the application signs only in the 'Primary Examiner' box.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for allowance — when and how to record
rubrics_metrics.description: If the record does not make clear the examiner’s reasons for allowing claims, the examiner may set forth such reasoning (37 CFR 1.104(e)); reasons should be specific when record is not explicit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons for allowance are intended to improve quality/reliability of issued patents and help public/patentee evaluate scope. Include at least (1) the major difference in the claims not found in prior art of record and (2) reasons why that difference is considered patentable over the prior art (if not otherwise clear). Avoid stock, meaningless statements and avoid using reasons to improperly narrow claims by special definitions unsupported by the description. Reasons may be included in an Office action rejecting other claims or in a separate communication; applicant may comment. Be accurate and precise to avoid misinterpretation (see Festo, and MPEP guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection after allowance — primary examiner approval
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim noted as allowable shall be rejected after allowance only with the approval of the primary examiner; exercise great care in authorizing such rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a new rejection applicable to allowed claims is discovered, prepare memorandum to TC Director requesting withdrawal from issue with rationale and new references. If approved, TC Director will withdraw and examiner prepares Office action reopening prosecution and citing new references. See MPEP § 706.07 for making the rejection final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when application withdrawn from issue
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is withdrawn from issue (by applicant or Office), the Office must mail/enter 'Notice of Withdrawal From Issue under 37 CFR 1.313(b)' signed/date-stamped and entered prior to issue date; update status and forward to examiner for appropriate action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office of Data Management updates status to remove issue data and place application in status 95. If the application contains an examiner’s amendment, the amended claims are subject to further examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Assurance reviews and reopening prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: OPQA conducts random quality reviews of Office actions; Review Quality Assurance Specialists independently review sampled actions for statutory compliance and may search as necessary. If a completed review finds one or more allowed claims unpatentable, prosecution will be reopened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality reviews are educational and used to improve practices; do not include quality review forms in Office actions or the application file; do not indicate a quality review occurred in the file record. Use form paragraphs 13.04/13.05 for reopening and vacating Notice of Allowance when applicable. If issue fee already paid, follow guidance for refunds or crediting deposit accounts and reapplication of issue fees when allowance is reissued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue of patent — electronic capture and issuance
rubrics_metrics.description: Once issue fee paid and post-allowance requirements met, application moves through IDC and FDC for electronic capture; effective sequencing by date issue fee paid; electronic patent issuance under USPTO seal implemented (as of Apr 18, 2023) and is considered a printed patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issue Notifications available electronically (or mailed for non-participants in e-Office action). Special handling for categories (made special by Director, priority >5 years old, reissue, interference-related, etc.). Refer to MPEP Chapter 1400 for issued patent corrections. Electronic grants include Director's digital signature and encrypted digital seal to authenticate (conformance with 35 U.S.C. 153 and 2(b)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing practitioner or firm names on patent
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee(s) Transmittal form (PTOL-85B) provides space for up to three registered patent attorneys/agents or a single firm name (with up to two attorney/agent names). If left blank, no practitioner/firm name will be printed on the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete item 2 on PTOL-85B to indicate printing preference; absence of entry results in no printed practitioner/firm name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment printing on patent
rubrics_metrics.description: PTOL-85B item 3 provides space for assignment data to comply with 37 CFR 3.81; assignment data printed on patent is based solely on PTOL-85B; if not provided, the patent will issue to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recording an assignment or submitting it for recordation per 37 CFR 3.11 is required for a patent to issue to an assignee. Provide assignment data on PTOL-85B to have assignee identified on the printed patent; for multiple names for same assignee only the first appearing name will be printed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printer rush cases — expedited handling
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Printer Rush' is indicated when documents must be addressed after allowance (RUSH document code); such applications are placed on expedited tab and taken up for immediate action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issues preventing publication include unresolved amendments under 1.312, inventorship corrections, or un-initialed IDS. Annotate RUSH document in Adobe with course of action; include annotated RUSH form in eRedFolder. If correction requires mailing an Office Action (Corrected Notice of Allowance, Response to Rule 312), include annotated RUSH in ERF; if no mailing required, create an action 'Printer Rush - No mailing' and scan annotated RUSH into file wrapper.
